estimates.label: 2024 ten-account annual local service-cost break-even threshold

period.label: Tax year 2024 equal-cost threshold for the ten active Siculus real-estate accounts

scope.label: Ten active Siculus real-estate PINs across their Polk County taxing jurisdictions; selected building unallocated

interval.interpretation: The threshold equals the exact 2024 ten-account paid-tax aggregation by definition; it is not observed or estimated public cost.

parameters.name: same_scope_recurring_real_property_tax_paid

provenance.detail: Exact arithmetic identity from the ten 2024 payment claims used by the companion combined-tax estimate

parameters.transformation: Used unchanged as the equal-cost threshold

estimates.confidence_rationale: The tax aggregation and threshold identity are exact, while actual same-scope marginal costs, PILOT/franchise receipts, incentive realization and recipient distributions remain unknown.
estimates.decision_relevance: States the annual public-cost level that would exactly offset the verified 2024 recurring real-property-tax base without fabricating a cost or fiscal surplus.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Annual marginal fire, police, road, water, wastewater, administrative, infrastructure and financing costs aligned to the ten accounts, recipient jurisdictions and tax year

derivation.formula: same-scope annual marginal public-service cost at break-even = sum of ten active-PIN 2024 property-tax payments = $2,249,854
assumptions: The threshold is an identity, not an observed or estimated public cost.
The hypothetical cost threshold uses the same ten-account and tax-year scope as the companion paid-tax aggregation.
Missing PILOT, franchise-fee, realized incentive and public-cost series motivate the threshold and are not reasons to omit it.
No projected PILOT, franchise estimate, maximum tax benefit, pump-station commitment, terminal bill, or current unpaid bill is added or netted.
No positive or negative fiscal margin is asserted without observed same-scope costs.

limitations: This is not an estimate of actual public-service cost.
The input is an account-level payment aggregation, not an audited recipient revenue ledger.
The ten-account scope is unallocated to the selected building and may omit personal property or temporary-building accounts.
A fiscal margin is positive only if actual same-scope marginal costs are below this threshold and negative only if above it; neither condition is established.
estimates.notes: Equal-cost identity only. Do not sum with the companion 2024 combined-tax estimate or present as public cost, avoided cost, fiscal benefit or net impact.

The result is campus-wide and unallocated to the selected building.

estimates.label: Reported construction-hours FTE-year equivalence

period.label: Cumulative 8.7 million construction work hours reported since 2013 through the release date

scope.label: Meta Altoona multi-building campus construction program through December 14, 2021

interval.interpretation: Deterministic equivalence using 2,080 hours per FTE-year; not observed FTE, unique workers, resident employment or simultaneous headcount.

parameters.name: reported_construction_work_hours

provenance.detail: Meta reports 8.7 million construction work hours since 2013

parameters.transformation: Divided by the FTE-year hours convention

parameters.name: hours_per_fte_year

provenance.detail: Forty hours per week for 52 weeks; denominator convention only

parameters.transformation: Converts cumulative work hours to standardized FTE-year equivalents

estimates.confidence_rationale: The reported cumulative hours anchor is project-specific and the conversion is deterministic, but the source figure may be rounded and does not identify people, phase timing, residence, employers or selected-building allocation.
estimates.decision_relevance: Makes the construction labor-time scale comparable across projects without relabeling it as unique jobs or local employment.

evidence_search.remaining_evidence_gap: Unrounded hours, phase/building allocation, worker identities, employers, residence, trade mix, payroll, benefits and annual timing

derivation.formula: 8,700,000 reported construction work hours / 2,080 hours per FTE-year = 4,182.692307692308 FTE-year equivalents
assumptions: The published 8.7 million hours are used as reported through December 14, 2021.
A 2,080-hour denominator is a standardization convention, not an observed schedule.
The result is cumulative across campus construction since 2013 and cannot be added to the separate projected average or peak worker counts.

limitations: Not unique workers, observed FTE, Iowa-resident job-years, simultaneous jobs or permanent employment.
No building or annual allocation is available.
The published 8.7 million-hour figure may be rounded.
estimates.notes: Labor-hour equivalence only; do not add to the 1,000-worker projection or 1,300-worker historical peak.

No benefits, bonuses, payroll taxes, overtime, stock compensation, contractor margin or residence share is added.
The 31- and 41-job award figures are not added to the 400-person operator figure.

limitations: Not observed Meta or contractor payroll, employee compensation, local-resident income or a statistical bound.
The source may combine employees and contractors and describes daily presence rather than annual-average FTE.
IEDA wage commitments apply to qualifying award jobs, not necessarily the full on-site population.
No selected-building allocation is available.
estimates.notes: Scenario only; do not add the 31- or 41-job award counts, infer headcount beyond the 400 anchor, or present as observed payroll.
